Clicks, about 2 to 3 minutes

  1. Open folder (or clone the URL), type the entry command, press Analyse.
  2. Watch the stepper; at Trace say “about a million calls”; at Rank say “measured, not guessed”.
  3. Click collatz_sequence_len: Guarded, 21.3x, 500/500 replays match. Diff: one decorator line.
  4. Journey tab: walk the stages (Section 2).
  5. Click problem_014: Declined 0.81x. “Careful, not reckless.”
  6. End-to-end card: 11.6x, output identical; original folder untouched.

If something fails

  1. Replay a saved run (no network): run docs\review3\demo\install_saved_runs.py, open /?job=c45cc4b3&replay=1.
  2. Local folder instead of the URL.
  3. TextLab (python main.py --small) or its saved run.

Before you go on stage

  • Laptop charged and plugged in
  • Installer rebuilt after this session’s runtime fixes (the one in dist/ is from 19 Oct)
  • No stale server on port 8765 (also check WSL)
  • Saved runs installed; dry run done this morning, cold and warm
  • Wi-Fi-off test passed; light theme; window at least 1440x900
Be honestThe main demo compiles one function and the repo has no licence file. If asked “why this repo”: it was the best small, unknown, pure-Python project that went through the real pipeline with identical output; most small repos use classes, generators or global state, which v1 declines with a stated reason.
Figure 10.1. The diff for the main demo: one decorator added, original body untouched.
numbers_row: 11.6xwhole-program speedup on the demo repository (dayyass/project-euler, problem 14), output identical
abstract_studio: Through the full Studio pipeline on a small public repository (dayyass/project-euler), a hot function ran 21.3x faster, verified on 500 of 500 recorded calls, and the whole program went from 8.9 s to 0.8 s with identical output.
conclusion_studio: On a third-party repository the system found the hot function, compiled it (21.3x), declined its caller on a measured 0.81x, and sped the program up 11.6x with identical output; on other candidates it found nothing worth compiling and said why, which is the intended behaviour.
latency_text: A cold Studio run took 51 s on the demo repository and 232 s on TextLab.
stress_text: The stress harness (`scripts/stress.py`) was **not re-run in this session**. The figures in `STATUS.md` (for example 17 of 17 files on one repository and 58 to 67% on three others, with zero converter crashes) were measured earlier on repositories the team had tuned on and are not reproduced here, so we make no stress-test claim. The independent evidence from this session is the demo-repository screening in `LIVE_DEMO.md`: about twenty small public repositories were cloned, five went through the full pipeline, and every function that was spliced matched CPython.
